results.content:
The latest generic congressional ballot polling continues to show Democrats with an edge nationally. RealClearPolling’s generic congressional vote tracker showed Democrats ahead of Republicans in the overall polling average by a 7-point margin.

However, this week's Economist/YouGov poll found there is still a strong contingent of undecided voters that could make all the difference between now and Election Day:

results.content:
This Economist/YouGov poll was conducted July 31 to Aug. 3 among 1,609 adults. The poll's margin of error was plus or minus 3.6 percentage points.

## Democrats’ performance

With Trump's continued unpopularity amongst the American public, Democrats have gained some ground politically, as they lead Republicans by 8 percentage points on a generic congressional ballot. In last week's Economist/YouGov poll, Democrats held a 4-point lead.
results.title: Trump's approval rating hovers near record lows despite improvement

results.content:
Democrats have built a lead over Republicans in the generic ballot before the midterm elections, when Republicans are working to maintain control of the House and Senate.

A national Economist/YouGov poll released Aug. 4 found 41% of Americans said they would vote for a Democratic candidate for Congress if the election were held today, compared to 33% who said they would vote for a Republican candidate.
results.title: Trump says voters are 'angry at Republicans,' not him, before midterms
